problems.title: Two Sum
problems.statement: Given an array of integers and a target, return the indices of the two numbers that add up to the target, in increasing order. Judged automatically: read the exact input/output format shown in the example.
hints: A hash map from value to index lets you check for the complement in one pass.
For each number, look up target - number before inserting the current number.

problems.title: Contains Duplicate
problems.statement: Given an array of integers, return true if any value appears at least twice, and false if every element is distinct. Judged automatically: read the exact input/output format shown in the example.
hints: A set tells you in O(1) whether you've seen a value before.

problems.title: Valid Anagram
problems.statement: Given two strings, return true if the second is an anagram of the first. Input: the two strings, one per line.
hints: Anagrams have identical letter-frequency counts.
Sorting both strings and comparing also works, just slower.

problems.title: Product of Array Except Self
problems.statement: Given an array, return an array where each element is the product of all the other elements, without using division. Input: the array on one line.
constraints: The product of any prefix/suffix fits in a 32-bit integer
hints: Compute the running product of everything to the left of i, then multiply in the running product of everything to the right of i.

problems.title: Maximum Subarray
problems.statement: Find the contiguous subarray with the largest sum and return that sum. Input: the array on one line.
hints: Kadane's algorithm: at each index, either extend the running subarray or start a new one there, whichever sum is larger.

problems.title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
problems.statement: Given an unsorted array of integers, return the length of the longest run of consecutive integers, in O(n) time. Input: the array on one line.
hints: Put every number in a set. Only start counting a sequence from a number whose predecessor (n-1) isn't in the set -- that guarantees each sequence is counted once.

problems.title: Valid Palindrome
problems.statement: Given a string, return true if it's a palindrome after lowercasing and removing all non-alphanumeric characters. Input: the string on one line.
problems.exampleInput: s = "A man, a plan, a canal: Panama"
hints: Walk two pointers inward from both ends, skipping non-alphanumeric characters as you go.

testCases.input: A man, a plan, a canal: Panama

problems.title: Container With Most Water
problems.statement: Given the heights of vertical lines, find two lines that together with the x-axis hold the most water, and return that area. Input: the heights on one line.
hints: Start with the widest container (both ends) and always move the pointer at the shorter line inward -- moving the taller one can never improve the area.

problems.title: Trapping Rain Water
problems.statement: Given elevation heights, compute how much rain water is trapped between the bars after it rains. Input: the heights on one line.
hints: The water above index i is min(maxToTheLeft, maxToTheRight) - height[i].
Track a running left-max and right-max with two pointers instead of precomputing arrays.

problems.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
problems.statement: Given daily prices, find the maximum profit from buying on one day and selling on a later day (0 if no profit is possible). Input: the prices on one line.
hints: Track the minimum price seen so far and the best profit seen so far in a single pass.

problems.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
problems.statement: Given a string, return the length of the longest substring without repeating characters. Input: the string on one line.
hints: Keep a window [start, end] and a map of the last index each character was seen at. When you see a repeat inside the window, jump start past its previous occurrence.

problems.title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
problems.statement: Given a string and an integer k, you may change up to k characters to any other character. Return the length of the longest substring of a single repeated letter you can get. Input: the string, then k on the next line.
hints: A window is valid whenever (window length) - (count of its most frequent letter) <= k.
Shrink the window from the left only when it becomes invalid; the max-frequency count never needs to decrease.

problems.title: Valid Parentheses
problems.statement: Given a string of just the characters '(', ')', '{', '}', '[' and ']', return true if every bracket is closed in the right order. Input: the string on one line.
hints: Push opening brackets. On a closing bracket, it must match the top of the stack, or the string is invalid.

problems.title: Evaluate Reverse Polish Notation
problems.statement: Evaluate an arithmetic expression given in Reverse Polish (postfix) Notation and return the integer result. Division truncates toward zero. Input: the space-separated tokens on one line.
hints: Push numbers. On an operator, pop the top two operands, apply the operator, and push the result back.

problems.title: Binary Search
problems.statement: Given a sorted array of distinct integers and a target, return its index, or -1 if it isn't present. Input: the sorted array, then the target on the next line.
constraints: nums is sorted in ascending order
hints: Compare the target against the middle element and discard half the search space each step.

problems.title: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array
problems.statement: A sorted array (with distinct values) was rotated at an unknown pivot. Return its minimum element in O(log n) time. Input: the array on one line.
hints: If the middle element is greater than the last element, the minimum is to its right; otherwise it's at mid or to the left.

problems.title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
problems.statement: A sorted array of distinct integers was rotated at an unknown pivot. Given a target, return its index or -1 in O(log n) time. Input: the array, then the target on the next line.
hints: One half of the array (from lo to mid, or mid to hi) is always properly sorted -- check whether the target lies in that sorted half to decide which way to go.

problems.title: Merge Intervals
problems.statement: Given a collection of intervals, merge all overlapping intervals and return them sorted by start. Input: n on the first line, then n lines of "start end".
hints: Sort by start time first. Then a new interval only needs to merge with the last one you've kept, never further back.

problems.title: Insert Interval
problems.statement: Given a sorted, non-overlapping list of intervals and a new interval, insert it and merge as needed. Input: n on the first line, n lines of "start end", then the new interval's "start end" on the last line.
hints: Copy every interval that ends before the new one starts, merge everything that overlaps it, then copy the rest.

problems.title: Non-overlapping Intervals
problems.statement: Given a set of intervals, return the minimum number you'd need to remove so none of the rest overlap. Input: n on the first line, then n lines of "start end".
hints: Sort by end time and greedily keep an interval only if it starts at or after the end of the last one you kept.

problems.title: Climbing Stairs
problems.statement: You can climb 1 or 2 steps at a time. Given n stairs, return how many distinct ways there are to reach the top. Input: n on one line.
hints: ways(n) = ways(n-1) + ways(n-2) -- it's Fibonacci with different base cases.

problems.title: Coin Change
problems.statement: Given coin denominations and a target amount, return the fewest coins needed to make that amount, or -1 if it's impossible. Input: the coin denominations, then the amount on the next line.
hints: Build up dp[a] = fewest coins for amount a, from dp[0] = 0 upward, trying every coin at each amount.

problems.title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
problems.statement: Given an integer array, return the length of its longest strictly increasing subsequence. Input: the array on one line.
hints: Maintain the smallest possible tail value for every achievable subsequence length; binary-search each new number into that list.

problems.title: House Robber
problems.statement: Given the amount of money in each house along a street, find the maximum you can rob without robbing two adjacent houses. Input: the amounts on one line.
hints: At each house, the best total is max(skip this house, rob it + best total two houses back).

problems.title: House Robber II
problems.statement: Same as House Robber, but the houses are arranged in a circle, so the first and last are adjacent. Input: the amounts on one line.
hints: Run House Robber twice: once excluding the first house, once excluding the last, and take the better result.

problems.title: Word Break
problems.statement: Given a string and a dictionary of words, return true if the string can be split into a sequence of dictionary words. Input: the string, then the dictionary words space-separated on the next line.
hints: dp[i] = true means s[0:i] can be fully segmented. dp[i] is true if some earlier dp[j] is true and s[j:i] is a dictionary word.

problems.title: Decode Ways
problems.statement: A message of digits maps 'A'-'Z' to 1-26. Given the encoded digit string, return how many ways it can be decoded. Input: the digit string on one line.
hints: dp[i] = ways to decode the first i characters. Add dp[i-1] if s[i-1] != '0', and dp[i-2] if the two-digit number s[i-2:i] is between 10 and 26.

problems.title: Unique Paths
problems.statement: A robot starts at the top-left of an m x n grid and can only move right or down. Return how many distinct paths reach the bottom-right. Input: m, then n on the next line.
hints: The number of ways to reach a cell is the sum of the ways to reach the cell above it and the cell to its left.

problems.title: Jump Game
problems.statement: Each element is the max jump length from that position. Starting at index 0, return true if you can reach the last index. Input: the array on one line.
hints: Track the farthest index reachable so far as you scan left to right; if you ever reach an index beyond that farthest point, you're stuck.

problems.title: Number of Islands
problems.statement: Given a grid of '1' (land) and '0' (water), return the number of islands, where an island is land connected horizontally/vertically. Input: rows and cols on the first line, then that many rows of space-separated 0/1 values.
hints: Flood-fill (DFS or BFS) from every unvisited land cell, sinking the whole island so it isn't counted again.

problems.title: Course Schedule
problems.statement: Given numCourses and prerequisite pairs [a, b] (take b before a), return true if it's possible to finish all courses (i.e., no cycle). Input: numCourses and the number of prerequisite pairs on the first line, then each pair "a b" on its own line.
hints: This is cycle detection on a directed graph -- repeatedly remove courses with no remaining prerequisites (topological sort/Kahn's algorithm); if every course gets removed, there's no cycle.

problems.title: Clone Graph
problems.statement: Given a reference node in a connected undirected graph, return a deep copy of the graph. Since a deep-copy can't be observed directly through stdout, instead: read an undirected graph as an edge list (nodes numbered 1..n), build a genuine deep copy of it, then print the copy's adjacency lists to demonstrate the copy is structurally correct. Input: n and m on the first line (m = number of edges), then m lines of "u v". Output: n lines, line i listing node i's neighbors sorted ascending, space-separated.
problems.exampleOutput: a deep-copied graph with the same structure
constraints: Typical LeetCode-scale limits for this problem
hints: A hash map from original node to cloned node prevents infinite loops and duplicate clones as you DFS/BFS.

problems.title: Pacific Atlantic Water Flow
problems.statement: Given a grid of heights, return the coordinates from which water can flow to both the Pacific and Atlantic oceans. Input: rows and cols on the first line, then that many rows of space-separated heights. Output each cell that can reach both oceans, sorted by row then column, as "row col" pairs one per line (0-indexed).
constraints: Typical LeetCode-scale limits for this problem
hints: Run a reverse flood-fill from all Pacific-adjacent and all Atlantic-adjacent cells; the intersection of the two reachable sets is the answer.

problems.title: Graph Valid Tree
problems.statement: Given n nodes and a list of undirected edges, return true if the edges form a valid tree (connected, no cycles). Input: n and m on the first line (m = number of edges, nodes 0-indexed), then m lines of "u v". Output true if the edges form a valid tree.
constraints: Typical LeetCode-scale limits for this problem
hints: A graph with n nodes is a tree exactly when it's connected and has exactly n - 1 edges.

problems.title: Number of Connected Components in an Undirected Graph
problems.statement: Given n nodes and a list of undirected edges, return the number of connected components. Input: n and m on the first line (m = number of edges, nodes 0-indexed), then m lines of "u v".
constraints: Typical LeetCode-scale limits for this problem
hints: Union-Find: union every edge's endpoints, then count how many distinct roots remain.

problems.title: Number of 1 Bits
problems.statement: Given an unsigned 32-bit integer, return the number of '1' bits it has (its Hamming weight). Input: the integer on one line.
constraints: The input is given as an unsigned 32-bit integer
hints: n & (n - 1) clears the lowest set bit -- count how many times you can do that before n becomes 0.

problems.title: Counting Bits
problems.statement: Given n, return an array of length n+1 where the i-th value is the number of 1 bits in i. Input: n on one line.
hints: bits[i] = bits[i >> 1] + (i & 1) -- reuse the answer for i with its last bit dropped.

problems.title: Reverse Bits
problems.statement: Reverse the bits of a given unsigned 32-bit integer and return the resulting unsigned integer. Input: the integer on one line.
constraints: The input is an unsigned 32-bit integer
hints: Build the result bit by bit: shift the result left, OR in the lowest bit of n, then shift n right, 32 times.

problems.title: Missing Number
problems.statement: Given an array containing n distinct numbers from 0 to n, return the one number missing from the range. Input: the array on one line.
hints: The sum of 0..n minus the actual sum of the array is exactly the missing number.

problems.title: Kth Largest Element in an Array
problems.statement: Given an unsorted array and an integer k, return the k-th largest element (the k-th largest in sorted order, not the k-th distinct one). Input: the array, then k on the next line.
hints: A min-heap of size k, keeping only the k largest values seen so far, gives you the answer at its root once you've scanned everything.

problems.title: Top K Frequent Elements
problems.statement: Given an integer array and an integer k, return the k most frequent elements. Input: the array, then k on the next line. Output the k most frequent elements sorted by frequency descending (ties broken by ascending value), space-separated.
hints: Bucket elements by frequency (index = frequency) and read off the top k buckets from the high end.

problems.title: Find Median from Data Stream
problems.statement: Design a structure that supports adding numbers one at a time and finding the median of all numbers added so far. Input: the number of operations k, then k lines each "add val" or "find". Output one line per "find", the median of all values added so far, printed with no trailing .0 for whole numbers where possible -- print as an integer when the median has no fractional part, otherwise with exactly one decimal place.
hints: Keep a max-heap for the lower half and a min-heap for the upper half, rebalanced so their sizes never differ by more than 1.

problems.title: Gas Station
problems.statement: There are n gas stations in a circle; gas[i] fuel is available and cost[i] is needed to reach the next station. Return the starting station index that lets you complete the circuit (guaranteed unique if it exists), or -1. Input: gas array, then cost array on the next line.
hints: If the total gas is less than the total cost, no solution exists.
Otherwise, whenever your running tank goes negative starting from some index, none of the stations up to and including that index can be the start -- restart from the next one.

problems.title: Reverse Linked List
problems.statement: Given the head of a singly linked list, reverse it and return the new head. Input: the list values, space-separated, in order.
constraints: The number of nodes is in the range [0, 5000]
hints: Walk the list once, re-pointing each node's `next` to the previous node as you go.

problems.title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
problems.statement: Merge two sorted linked lists into one sorted list by splicing their nodes together. Input: two sorted lists, one per line, space-separated (an empty line means an empty list).
constraints: The number of nodes in both lists is in the range [0, 50]
hints: Use a dummy head node and repeatedly attach whichever list's current node is smaller.

problems.title: Linked List Cycle
problems.statement: Given a linked list, determine if it has a cycle. Input: the list values, space-separated, then the 0-indexed position the tail connects back to on the next line (-1 for no cycle).
constraints: The number of nodes is in the range [0, 10^4]
hints: Floyd's cycle detection: a slow pointer and a fast pointer will eventually meet if and only if there's a cycle.

problems.title: Remove Nth Node From End of List
problems.statement: Given the head of a list and an integer n, remove the n-th node from the end and return the head. Input: the list values, space-separated, then n on the next line. Output the resulting list's values space-separated on one line (an empty line if the list becomes empty).
constraints: The number of nodes is in the range [1, 30]
hints: Advance a lead pointer n steps ahead first, then move both pointers together until the lead reaches the end.

problems.title: Reorder List
problems.statement: Given a list L0-L1-...-Ln, reorder it in place to L0-Ln-L1-Ln-1-... Input: the list values, space-separated.
constraints: The number of nodes is in the range [1, 5 * 10^4]
hints: Find the middle (slow/fast pointers), reverse the second half, then merge the two halves alternately.

problems.title: Merge k Sorted Lists
problems.statement: Given k sorted linked lists, merge them into one sorted list. Input: k on the first line, then k lines each a sorted list, space-separated (an empty line means an empty list).
hints: A min-heap of the current head of each list lets you always pull the next-smallest node in O(log k).

problems.title: Invert Binary Tree
problems.statement: Given the root of a binary tree, swap every left/right child pair and return the root. Input: the tree, level-order, space-separated, using "null" for missing children.
constraints: The number of nodes is within typical LeetCode limits for this problem
hints: Recursively invert the left and right subtrees, then swap them.

problems.title: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
problems.statement: Given the root of a binary tree, return its maximum depth (number of nodes along the longest root-to-leaf path). Input: the tree, level-order, space-separated, using "null" for missing children.
constraints: The number of nodes is within typical LeetCode limits for this problem
hints: The depth is 1 + the larger of the two subtrees' depths (0 for a null node).

problems.title: Same Tree
problems.statement: Given the roots of two binary trees, return true if they are structurally identical with the same node values. Input: two trees, one per line, each level-order space-separated using "null" for missing children.
constraints: The number of nodes is within typical LeetCode limits for this problem
hints: Two trees match if their roots match and both pairs of subtrees match recursively.

problems.title: Subtree of Another Tree
problems.statement: Given two binary trees, return true if the second is a subtree of the first (identical to some node's whole subtree). Input: the root tree, then the candidate subtree, one per line, each level-order space-separated using "null" for missing children.
constraints: The number of nodes is within typical LeetCode limits for this problem
hints: At every node of the main tree, check whether the subtree rooted there is the Same Tree as subRoot.

problems.title: Validate Binary Search Tree
problems.statement: Given the root of a binary tree, return true if it is a valid binary search tree. Input: the tree, level-order, space-separated, using "null" for missing children.
constraints: The number of nodes is within typical LeetCode limits for this problem
hints: Carry a valid (low, high) range down through the recursion -- a node's value must fit strictly inside it.

problems.title: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal
problems.statement: Given the root of a binary tree, return the values of its nodes level by level, left to right. Input: the tree, level-order, space-separated, using "null" for missing children. Output one line per depth level, values space-separated.
constraints: The number of nodes is within typical LeetCode limits for this problem
hints: A BFS queue naturally processes one level at a time if you track how many nodes are currently in the queue.

problems.title: Kth Smallest Element in a BST
problems.statement: Given the root of a BST and an integer k, return the k-th smallest value in it. Input: the tree, level-order space-separated using "null" for missing children, then k on the next line.
constraints: The number of nodes is within typical LeetCode limits for this problem
hints: An in-order traversal of a BST visits nodes in ascending order -- stop at the k-th one.

problems.title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a BST
problems.statement: Given a BST and two of its nodes, return their lowest common ancestor. Input: the tree, level-order space-separated using "null" for missing children, then p's value, then q's value, each on its own line.
constraints: The number of nodes is within typical LeetCode limits for this problem
hints: Walk down from the root: if both values are less than the current node, go left; if both are greater, go right; otherwise you've found the split point.

problems.title: Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum
problems.statement: Given a binary tree, return the maximum sum of any path between any two nodes (the path need not pass through the root). Input: the tree, level-order, space-separated, using "null" for missing children.
constraints: The number of nodes is within typical LeetCode limits for this problem
hints: For each node, compute the best sum going down into just one child (what you can return upward) versus the best sum using both children as a 'peak' (a candidate for the global answer).

problems.title: Serialize and Deserialize Binary Tree
problems.statement: Design an algorithm to serialize a binary tree to a string and deserialize it back to the original tree. Input: the tree, level-order space-separated using "null" for missing children (trailing null-only levels omitted), or the single token "null" for an empty tree. Output your serialized form of the tree you deserialized -- it should exactly match the input's canonical form (same level-order + null convention, trailing null-only levels omitted).
constraints: The number of nodes is within typical LeetCode limits for this problem
hints: A pre-order traversal that explicitly writes a marker for null children can be deserialized unambiguously by consuming tokens in the same order.

problems.title: Construct Binary Tree from Preorder and Inorder Traversal
problems.statement: Given the preorder and inorder traversal of a binary tree with unique values, reconstruct and return the tree. Input: the preorder sequence, then the inorder sequence, one per line, space-separated (values are distinct). Output the reconstructed tree, level-order, space-separated, using "null" for missing children (trailing null-only levels omitted).
constraints: The number of nodes is within typical LeetCode limits for this problem
hints: The first element of preorder is always the root; its position in inorder splits the left and right subtrees.

problems.title: Implement Trie (Prefix Tree)
problems.statement: Implement a Trie with insert, search, and startsWith operations. Input: the number of operations k, then k lines each "insert word", "search word", or "startsWith prefix". Output one line per search/startsWith operation (insert produces no output), "true" or "false".
problems.exampleInput: insert("apple"); search("apple") -> true; search("app") -> false; startsWith("app") -> true
hints: Each Trie node holds a map/array of children plus a flag for 'a word ends here'.

testCases.input:
6
insert apple
search apple
search app
startsWith app
insert app
search app

problems.title: Design Add and Search Words Data Structure
problems.statement: Design a data structure that supports adding words and searching, where a search word may contain '.' to match any letter. Input: the number of operations k, then k lines each "addWord word" or "search pattern" (pattern may contain '.' as a single-character wildcard). Output one line per search operation (addWord produces no output), "true" or "false".
hints: Build it on top of a Trie; when you hit a '.', recursively try every child at that level instead of just one.

testCases.input:
7
addWord bad
addWord dad
addWord mad
search pad
search bad
search .ad
search b..

problems.title: Combination Sum
problems.statement: Given distinct candidate numbers and a target, return all unique combinations that sum to the target (numbers may repeat). Input: the candidates array, then the target on the next line (candidates may repeat in a combination). Output every combination, ascending values space-separated, one per line, in the order produced by the standard sorted-candidates start-index backtracking algorithm (try candidates from the current index onward, non-decreasing).
constraints: Typical LeetCode-scale limits for this problem
hints: Recurse with a running sum and a 'start' index so you never reuse an earlier candidate, which avoids duplicate combinations.

problems.title: Word Search
problems.statement: Given a grid of letters and a word, return true if the word can be formed by moving between adjacent cells without reusing one. Input: rows and cols on the first line, then that many rows of space-separated single-character cells, then the word to find on the last line.
constraints: Typical LeetCode-scale limits for this problem
hints: DFS from every cell that matches the word's first letter, marking cells visited and unmarking them on backtrack.

testCases.input:
3 4
A B C E
S F C S
A D E E
ABCCED

3 4
A B C E
S F C S
A D E E
ABCB

problems.title: Subsets
problems.statement: Given an array of unique integers, return all possible subsets (the power set). Input: the array, space-separated (values are distinct). Output every subset, ascending values space-separated (an empty line for the empty subset), one per line, in the order produced by the standard start-index backtracking algorithm: beginning from the empty subset, extend the current subset by trying each next unused index in increasing order, recording the subset immediately at each choice before backtracking.
constraints: Typical LeetCode-scale limits for this problem
hints: At each element, branch into two recursive calls: one that includes it, one that doesn't.

problems.title: Permutations
problems.statement: Given an array of distinct integers, return all possible permutations. Input: the array, space-separated (values are distinct). Output every permutation, space-separated, one per line, in the order produced by the standard visited-array backtracking algorithm: at each position, try unused elements in their original array order.
constraints: Typical LeetCode-scale limits for this problem
hints: Swap each remaining element into the current position and recurse, then swap back to try the next one.
